subject: PASS: artifact identity, producer identity, and transport identity remain orthogonal

proof: A DSSE/result-bundle digest binds canonical artifact content and signature material; it does not establish that the workflow or producer definition that generated it was trusted. #3880 exists precisely because project-side re-execution is an independent observer rather than a consequence of artifact identity.

The owned Bonfÿre trace-verifier fix separately normalizes provider identity for digest/fidelity comparisons, demonstrating that semantic producer claims require their own comparison boundary rather than being inferred from content addressing.

Bernstein #3863/#3883 explicitly define one signed versioned protocol carried by several transports. GitHub is the default transport, not the semantic foundation; hub HTTPS and future discovery transports carry the same documents and therefore cannot inherit protocol authority merely from transport-local identity.

counterexamples.example: An attacker-controlled workflow can produce a structurally valid, correctly hashed DSSE envelope. Artifact verification may pass while project-side clean-room execution disagrees with its claimed gate outcome. The correct state is authenticated artifact plus untrusted/divergent producer observation, not trusted work.

The same signed submission document may arrive through a GitHub PR, a hub HTTPS lease flow, or a mirrored registry. PR number, hub lease id, URL, retry metadata, and transport timestamps may change without changing the protocol document digest or its authority semantics.

body.regression_fence: ReceiptEnvelope/EvidenceGraph must represent artifact/content identity, producer/workflow identity, and transport/session identity as separately typed evidence edges. No one edge may be promoted into either of the other two without an explicit verifier observation.
